description: Discriminator: a replica owning instance (0,0) whose record was created by a recovery-led PreAccept receives a legal NOOP Commit. Prefix: the harness runs the real handlePreAccept (creating the record without bookkeeping) and then the real handleCommit. Controls: the same events print whether bookkeeping was nil, the status after the PreAccept, whether the handler panicked, the panic value and whether the commit had any effect, so a mis-built record is visible.

harness.description: In-package Go test that creates the message-made record with the real handler and then delivers a legal NOOP Commit, recovering the panic so the observation is reported instead of killing the test process.
semantic_changes: harness-only scaffolding: the Replica is constructed in-package, peer writers are buffers, and the two handlers are called directly; the handlers are unmodified
the harness wraps the commit delivery in recover() purely to observe a panic; production runs the handler inside the run loop where no recover exists

legality.derivation: Both messages are the ones the protocol sends for a recovery-led NOOP: a PreAccept at the recovery ballot and the Commit for the resulting instance.
legality.applicability: One instance, one commit, direct handler calls.
unresolved: the production dispatcher's treatment of a panicking handler is not modelled

grounding.derivation: The event reports whether the handler panicked and whether the commit had an effect, which is the observable form of the duty.
grounding.applicability: The record existed without bookkeeping and the commit was well formed.

observable_properties.description: Delivering a legal NOOP commit for an instance the replica owns must not terminate the handler.

uncertainties: the harness observes the panic rather than the replica process terminating, since the run loop is not driven
the client-side and history sides of the NOOP recovery are outside this check
